title: Post-done named-root release returns 'superseded authority image' instead of a clear lifecycle result
outcome: Clarify and correctly implement releasing an item's named source root after completion: distinguish an already ended binding from a stale authority image, without granting mutation after a claim ends.
acceptance: The cause is recorded from code and this occurrence. It says what `done` does to the item's named source root binding (ends it, keeps it, or leaves it for release), and why a release after `done` returned the 'superseded authority image' 409 instead of a lifecycle result.

A named-root release after `done` returns a clear, definite lifecycle result. Either it succeeds idempotently with 'already ended by completion' when completion has ended the binding, or it refuses with a named reason that says what the caller should do. No mutation authority is granted after the claim has ended, and a genuinely stale authority image is still refused as today.

Deterministic tests cover: release after `done` (binding already ended); release after `done` when completion leaves the binding open (if that state exists); and a genuinely stale authority image. The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input.

completion.summary: Landed post-completion own-clear lifecycle results in d3499b97, preserving stale authority refusals; deterministic regressions, independent reviews and both exact-tree full gates pass.
